title: What’s the latest on UK university compliance?
summary_en: This week, The PIE held the inaugural Compliance Con, bringing together compliance experts from across the UK sector. As tightened BCA thresholds loom, editor Beth Kennedy unpacks key takeaways from the event.
author: The PIE News team
title_cn: What’s the latest on UK university compliance?

title: Amaral Cunha, Escola Eleva
summary_en: This week, The PIE sat down with Amaral Cunha, head of school at Escola Eleva, part of Inspired Education Group. We spoke about his career to date and education's power to transform communities.
author: The PIE News team

title: Alphabetti spaghetti and Australia’s international education policy problem
summary_en: Neil Fitzroy explores how a growing maze of acronyms, restrictions and visa uncertainty may be undermining Australia's appeal as a study destination.
author: Neil Fitzroy
title_cn: Alphabetti spaghetti and Australia’s international education policy problem

title: Student with gun demands deposit refund from agent
summary_en: A major study abroad agent has told The PIE it was forced to close offices in Pakistan for more than 10 days after a man with a gun demanded a refund of his  tuition fee deposit after being refused a visa to study in the UK.
author: Nicholas Cuthbert
title_cn: Student with gun demands deposit refund from agent

title: Universities Australia warns against growing regulatory burden under Albanese reforms
summary_en: Universities Australia chief executive Luke Sheehy has warned that growing regulation and political intervention is weighing on universities, urging the new tertiary education commission to simplify oversight rather than add to it.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Universities Australia warns against growing regulatory burden under Albanese reforms

title: German chancellor casts doubt on US study amid “different social climate”
summary_en: Friedrich Merz says he would not currently recommend young people study or work in the US, as debates around employability, stability and global student mobility intensify.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: German chancellor casts doubt on US study amid “different social climate”

title: UK study visa issuance falls 32%
summary_en: UK study visa issuance in Q1 2026 is down by a third compared to last year, as new government figures show net migration plummet.
author: Polly Nash

title: Jacqui Smith hails UK ELT as English UK warns policy progress must not “stall”
summary_en: Skills minister Jacqui Smith has hailed English language teaching as a “very important strand” of the UK’s international education strategy, as English UK urges the government to accelerate reforms on youth mobility.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Jacqui Smith hails UK ELT as English UK warns policy progress must not “stall”

title: “Open campuses, joint degrees”: Canada envoy signals India push
summary_en: Canada’s high commissioner to India says Canadian institutions are preparing for a deeper presence in India through branch campuses, joint degrees and talent partnerships, as the two countries rebuild education ties amid falling student mobility.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: “Open campuses, joint degrees”: Canada envoy signals India push

title: Trump backs Chinese students as US confidence wanes
summary_en: Following President Trump’s unexpected remarks about the value of Chinese students to US colleges, experts say rhetoric is not enough to restore Chinese families’ and students’ faith in America as a study destination.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: Trump backs Chinese students as US confidence wanes

title: India’s smaller cities fuel Germany’s popularity as students rethink study abroad
summary_en: Stakeholders say students from India’s tier-II and III cities are increasingly turning to Germany for its affordability, employability and migration pathways, even as concerns around visas, language and housing persist.
author: Abhishek Nair
title_cn: India’s smaller cities fuel Germany’s popularity as students rethink study abroad

title: Malala seeks urgent action from ministers on girls’ education gap
summary_en: Malala Yousafzai used her platform at the Education World Forum (EWF) to remind ministers that 122 million girls remain out of school worldwide, and each year of delay in policy and funding decisions is "a year of school that a child will never get back".
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Malala seeks urgent action from ministers on girls’ education gap

title: K-12: international schools call for global safeguarding overhaul
summary_en: International school associations and safeguarding experts have found what they describe as a major loophole in international teacher accountability.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: K-12: international schools call for global safeguarding overhaul

title: Australian budget puts research and skills in focus
summary_en: Australia’s federal budget has drawn a mixed response across the sector, with universities, TAFEs and research leaders broadly welcoming continuity in skills and innovation policy, while warning that funding pressures and reform gaps remain unresolved.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Australian budget puts research and skills in focus
